title: Evaluating LLM Apps and Agents: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on building eval datasets, measuring retrieval and answer quality, using LLM judges safely, evaluating agent trajectories, and gating changes with regression suites in CI.

chapters.title: Evaluation Mental Model and Dataset Building
points: Evals are unit tests for non-deterministic systems: fixed inputs, scored outputs, tracked over time so changes are measured, not guessed
Evaluate components separately (retriever, generator, agent steps) and end to end; an overall score alone cannot locate the failing stage
Golden dataset record: input, reference answer or expected facts, gold source doc IDs, tags (category, difficulty)
Sources, best first: real production logs, expert-written cases, synthetic LLM-generated cases (always human-spot-check them)

Cover edge cases on purpose: unanswerable questions, ambiguous queries, adversarial inputs, and rare categories; 50-200 curated cases beat thousands of noisy ones; keep a held-out split to avoid overfitting prompts to the set

chapters.title: Retrieval Metrics: Recall@k, MRR and Friends
points: Recall@k = relevant docs found in top k / total relevant docs; measures whether the answer evidence reached the generator
Precision@k = relevant docs in top k / k; low precision means noisy context that distracts the model
MRR = mean over queries of 1/rank of the first relevant hit; rank 1 gives 1.0, rank 4 gives 0.25, a miss gives 0
MRR cares only about the first hit; nDCG handles graded relevance and rewards ranking several good docs high
Worked example: gold doc at rank 3 for query A and rank 1 for query B gives MRR = (1/3 + 1)/2 ≈ 0.67; recall@k rises with k, so pick k to match the context you actually pass in

chapters.title: Answer Faithfulness and Relevance
points: Faithfulness (groundedness): every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved context; it detects hallucination
Measure it by splitting the answer into atomic claims, then checking each claim against the context; score = supported claims / total claims
Answer relevance: does the answer actually address the question, regardless of whether it is true
Context relevance: how much of the retrieved context was useful for the question; it separates retrieval failures from generation failures

A faithful answer can still be irrelevant, and a relevant answer can be unfaithful; low recall with low faithfulness means fix retrieval first, high recall with low faithfulness means fix the prompt or model

chapters.title: LLM-as-Judge: Rubrics and Biases
points: Use a judge model to score open-ended outputs when exact match fails; the judge prompt is a spec you must test like any other code
Rubric design: one criterion per judge call, explicit score anchors (what a 1, 3 and 5 look like), reasoning before the score, structured JSON output, temperature 0
Pairwise comparison is more reliable than absolute scoring, but run both orders and count a disagreement as a tie
Known biases: position bias (prefers the first answer), verbosity bias (prefers longer), self-preference (favors its own model family), and weak on hard math or factual checks

Calibrate by comparing the judge with human labels on 30-100 cases (agreement rate or Cohen's kappa); use a different or stronger model than the one being judged; re-calibrate whenever the judge prompt or model changes

chapters.title: Agent Trajectory Evaluation and CI Regression Suites
points: Trajectory = the ordered steps of an agent run (thoughts, tool calls, arguments, observations); score the path, not just the final answer
Trajectory metrics: tool selection correctness, argument validity, step efficiency (steps vs optimal), loops or redundant calls, and task success rate
Match modes against a reference trajectory: exact, in-order, any-order; prefer outcome checks (final state, such as the DB row created) over exact paths since many valid routes exist
Regression suite in CI: run a small fast subset on every PR and the full set nightly; cache or mock tools and fix the seed to cut flakiness and cost
Gate merges on thresholds per metric (for example recall@5 must not drop more than 2 points versus main); promote every production failure into a new test case; pin judge model and version

chapters.title: Evals Cheat Sheet
points: Dataset: input + reference + gold doc IDs + tags; mine production logs; include unanswerable cases; keep a held-out split
Retrieval: recall@k (found?), precision@k (noise?), MRR = mean(1/rank of first hit), nDCG for graded relevance
Generation: faithfulness = supported claims / total claims, answer relevance, context relevance
Judge: one criterion per call, anchored rubric, reasoning first, temp 0, swap order, calibrate against human labels
Biases: position, verbosity, self-preference; agents: score tool choice, arguments, efficiency, outcome; CI: fast PR subset, nightly full run, threshold gates
